Hi Jason / Nimbus team,

Thanks for taking the time today — really helpful call. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of your constraints
- Primary: keep conversational p95 latency under ~120ms for 95% of requests during business-hours peaks.
- Peak: expect ~150–250 requests/sec for the symptom-check flow during peak minutes (burst safe to 300/sec).
- Typical prompt sizes: ~800–2,000 tokens (longer contextual history + user input).
- Multi-region: US-first, possible EU later; multi-region routing may be needed for DR.

Initial recommendation (high level)
- Dedicated capacity looks like the best fit if you need predictable p95 under 120ms at sustained 200+ rps. Hosted API can work for lower/variable traffic or as a staging path, but it will be harder to guarantee throughput SLOs during peak without reservation.

Next steps
1) Can you confirm expected average token length and the percent of requests that hit the 1.5–2k token range? (this affects sizing).
2) I’ll send an initial Dedicated sizing proposal and our latency benchmark report so you can see numbers for similar workloads.
3) If you’re open, we can schedule a 1-hour sizing review + a 1-day synthetic load test on a Dedicated pool (we can spin a trial pod for that).

Attaching a short checklist and I’ll follow up with the sizing doc.

Jason — great questions, answered inline and with attachments.

1) Benchmarks for 1.8–2k tokens
- We ran comparable public-model benchmarks for 2k tokens on our Dedicated pools (A100/H100-class instances) with continuous batching knobs tuned. Typical p95 observed: ~90–140ms for streaming-first-byte on our optimized stacks depending on model family and quantization (smaller families are faster).
- I’m attaching a short benchmark report that shows p50/p95/p99 at different seq lengths across model variants. See "redwood-benchmark-latency-report.pdf".

2) Hosted -> Dedicated migration path
- API: identical surface. Same endpoints, same SDKs.
- Data: Dedicated gives you isolation and reserved GPUs (predictable throughput). We support pinning model versions and have a config layer to switch traffic from hosted to dedicated with minimal code changes.
- Risk: Hosted is quicker to start and lower commitment; however, no guaranteed throughput at peak without reserved capacity. Migration to Dedicated is straightforward from an integration standpoint, but scheduling the Dedicated pool requires lead time for reserved capacity.

Sizing proposal (high level)
- For your mix and peak of 200–250 rps with ~10% at 1.8–2k tokens, we’d propose a Dedicated pool configured for sustained 250 rps headroom. The attached "dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf" has an example config and estimated cost.
- Recommended initial trial: 48-hour Dedicated trial with synthetic traffic that mirrors your token distribution so you can validate p95 and throughput. We can allocate a trial pool under DEAL-8342.

Security docs
- Attaching SOC2 summary and our compliance starter pack: "SOC2-summary.pdf". We can also provide network diagrams and an SOC2 report on NDA / procurement stage.

Next steps
- I can schedule the 1-hour sizing review with our infra leads — proposed times: Thu 6/24 9am or 10:30am PT.
- If that looks good, we’ll book the 48-hour trial and run the synthetic test.

Thanks — attaching the two reports now.

Best,
Neha
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-latency-report.pdf, dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf
